configuration: LightMem-Ego online runtime as described in arXiv 2607.11487v1 and implemented under src/backend plus the Rokid glasses Android client (src/ai_glass_app) and web/phone-browser client (src/frontend): continuous frame+audio streaming into the three-tier memory (M_cur current, M_st short-term micro-events, M_lt long-term episodic/semantic built by EM2Mem), with the memory router / retrieval / evidence-grounded experience QA path. The offline EM2Mem benchmark pipeline under research/em2mem (EgoLife, Video-MME) is not the judged configuration.

S->M.label: reported
S->M.rationale: Sensed frames and audio chunks uploaded by the glasses/phone client are written into current and short-term memory and, after rolling ASR and refinement, consolidated into long-term memory; transcripts are backfilled onto existing segments. User-supplied corrections also reach memory: the web client can rewrite 30-second episodic records through PUT /session/{id}/memories/30sec, after which the service re-derives multiscale, graph and semantic memory from the edited records (online_memory_edit/service.py). Both the paper and the code describe the implemented write path.

M->A.label: reported
M->A.rationale: Answering is explicitly memory-grounded: a keyword router chooses which memory tiers to retrieve from, retrieved event records, transcripts, frames and semantic facts are fused into an evidence view, and the answer is generated from that view. The retained interaction cache also feeds the routing decision (M_cache priority, follow-up time routing). Implemented in the query engine and router.

A->S.label: insufficient
A->S.rationale: No flow from Action to Sensing is described. The client captures frames on a fixed interval and audio in fixed chunks independent of any query or answer state (reserveFrameCapture only checks FRAME_INTERVAL_MS), and the ask path reads already-stored M_cur/M_st/M_lt and open-event state without requesting a capture, an ASR flush, or an event refine; the only on-demand close/refine trigger sits in the stream-end endpoint invoked when the user stops capture (api_server.py lines 3999-4004). No expected-effect checks on delivered answers exist. The paper describes the capture layer as a lightweight forwarder but does not explicitly exclude action-guided sensing, so the route is unknown rather than excluded.

M->S.label: reported
M->S.rationale: Retained dialogue state (recent interactions, hot entities, hot time ranges; persisted in em2mem/cache/interaction_cache.json with 20-turn / 3600 s retention) is supplied to a rule-based coreference resolver that interprets the incoming user question before any retrieval: pronoun or follow-up questions are rewritten into a resolved question carrying the prior entities and time ranges, and that resolved question is what retrieval then consumes. This is retained priors guiding interpretation of current input, distinct from answer-time retrieval. Caveat: no memory priors reach the frame/audio side (frame-diff detection, captioner and refiner prompts contain only the segment's own keyframes and transcript, vlm_captioner.py lines 24-40, micro_event_refiner.py lines 31-45), and the paper itself does not describe this step; the evidence is code-only.
M->S.quote: Code (verified): """Lightweight rule-based follow-up/coreference resolver."""; "resolved_question = (f\"Using the previous context\" f\"{self._entity_clause(entity_names)}\" f\"{self._time_clause(range_text)}, answer: {q}\")"; "cache_context = CoreferenceResolver().resolve(question, self.interaction_cache)"

A->M.label: reported
A->M.rationale: After each successful answer the service writes its own utterance and action context into retained stores: the interaction cache turn record holds the question, resolved question, answer, route_decision, retrieved memory/segment ids and evidence frames, and merges hot entities/time ranges for later turns; every question/answer with status, client source, input method and task id is appended to qa_history.jsonl (served back via GET /session/{id}/qa_history and loaded by the web client); a query_answered event is appended to the session timeline. The paper does not mention this; evidence is code-only.

record.label: stated
record.rationale: The service keeps records of what it decided and delivered for its own later use: the persisted interaction cache stores each answered turn (answer, route decision, retrieved ids, evidence frames) and is read by the coreference resolver and router on subsequent questions; qa_history.jsonl records every question/answer with status and client source and is served to the web client. These are runtime records used by the service, not author-only trial logs (the separate eval export in scripts/build_session_eval.py is author-only and not relied on here). The paper text itself does not describe this recording.

outcome.label: not_stated
outcome.rationale: No later evidence about delivered answers (rating, dismissal, correction, receipt, task result) is obtained or retained: a repository-wide search finds no feedback/rating endpoint or UI, the glasses client only displays and plays the answer, and later user turns are stored in the interaction cache only as fresh dialogue context with no link to the prior answer as an outcome. The 30-second memory editor corrects memory records, not answers, and the paper lists user-controlled memory editing only as future work; LLM-judge/human accuracy in Sec. 5.3 is offline author scoring.

attribution.label: not_stated
attribution.rationale: No outcome is captured, so nothing is linked back to a decision to check or correct assistance; the only answer scoring is the authors' offline LLM-judge and human evaluation over 27 queries (Sec. 5.3), which does not count.

revision.label: not_stated
revision.rationale: The service makes no durable change to its own mechanism: captioner/refiner system prompts are fixed string constants, the router's keyword tables are static class attributes, and no parameters, rules, skills or code are updated from experience. Semantic memory of routines/preferences and edited episodic records are content consumed by a fixed mechanism, and memory edits are written by the user. The paper's Limitations section itself says the memory update mechanism lacks any revising policy.

notes: Judged the online LightMem-Ego runtime (phone/glasses client + src/backend three-tier memory + experience QA), not the offline research/em2mem benchmark pipeline. Paper text was obtained through WebFetch (a summarizing tool), so every paper quote is marked UNVERIFIED; all code quotes were read directly from the checked-out commit and are verbatim. The paper describes S->M and M->A explicitly; the interaction cache (A->M write, M->S read for follow-up interpretation, M->A for routing) and qa_history recording exist only in code and are not mentioned in the paper. M->S is reported solely on the coreference resolver's use of retained dialogue state to reinterpret user questions; no memory priors guide frame/audio sensing. A->S is left insufficient because the fixed-rate capture loop and ask path show no action-guided sensing, but the sources do not explicitly exclude it. No answer-feedback, attribution, or self-revision mechanism exists; the Limitations section confirms the memory update policy is preliminary.
